theory.intro: Two lines are **parallel** when they never meet, running with the same steepness. On the Cartesian plane, two lines are parallel exactly when their gradients are equal. So to test a pair of lines, find each gradient and compare.
facts: Two distinct lines with equal gradients are parallel.
In the form $y = mx + c$ the gradient is the coefficient $m$, so two lines are parallel when their $m$ values match.
Gradients written differently can still be equal: $\frac{2}{3}$ and $\frac{4}{6}$ are the same gradient, so those lines are parallel.
Two lines with the same gradient and the same $y$-intercept are the same line, not a parallel pair.
A line parallel to a given line has the same gradient and a different intercept.
steps: Find the gradient of each line.
Compare the gradients: equal gradients mean the lines are parallel.

mastery.question_text:
Which two of the lines $y = 2x + 1$ (blue), $y = 3x - 2$ (red) and $y = 2x - 4$ (green) are parallel?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6cm,height=5.4cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={-{Stealth}},xmin=-3,xmax=3,ymin=-7,ymax=7,xtick={-2,0,2},ytick={-6,-4,-2,0,2,4,6},grid=both,clip=false,scaled ticks=false,ticklabel style={font=\small,/pgf/number format/fixed},xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$}]\addplot[thick,blue,<->,domain=-3:2.9,samples=2] {2*x+1};\addplot[thick,red,dotted,<->,domain=-1.6:2.9,samples=2] {3*x-2};\addplot[thick,green!60!black,dashed,<->,domain=-1:3,samples=2] {2*x-4};\node[blue,above left] at (axis cs:2.4,5.8) {$y=2x+1$};\node[red,right] at (axis cs:2.0,4.4) {$y=3x-2$};\node[green!60!black,below right] at (axis cs:2.9,1.8) {$y=2x-4$};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
mastery.solution_text:
$y=2x+1$ has gradient $2$.
$y=3x-2$ has gradient $3$.
$y=2x-4$ has gradient $2$.
The two lines with equal gradients are $y=2x+1$ and $y=2x-4$, so these are the parallel pair.
[tikz]

mastery.question_text:
Line $A$ has equation $y = \frac{2}{3}x + 1$.
Line $B$ passes through $(0,-2)$ and $(3,0)$.
Are the lines parallel?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6cm,height=5.4cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={-{Stealth}},xmin=-3,xmax=6,ymin=-5,ymax=5,xtick={-2,0,2,4,6},ytick={-4,-2,0,2,4},grid=both,clip=false,scaled ticks=false,ticklabel style={font=\small,/pgf/number format/fixed},xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$}]\addplot[thick,blue,<->,domain=-3:5.4,samples=2] {(2/3)*x+1};\addplot[thick,red,dashed,<->,domain=-3:6,samples=2] {(2/3)*x-2};\addplot[only marks,mark=*,mark size=2pt,red] coordinates {(0,-2) (3,0)};\node[blue,above left] at (axis cs:3.6,3.4) {$A$};\node[red,below right] at (axis cs:4.6,1.1) {$B$};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
mastery.solution_text:
Gradient of $B=\frac{0-(-2)}{3-0}=\frac{2}{3}$.
Line $A$ has gradient $\frac{2}{3}$.
The gradients are equal, so the lines are parallel.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6cm,height=5.4cm,axis lines=middle,axis line style={-{Stealth}},xmin=-3,xmax=6,ymin=-5,ymax=5,xtick={-2,0,2,4,6},ytick={-4,-2,0,2,4},grid=both,clip=false,scaled ticks=false,ticklabel style={font=\small,/pgf/number format/fixed},xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$}]\addplot[thick,blue,<->,domain=-3:5.4,samples=2] {(2/3)*x+1};\addplot[thick,red,dashed,<->,domain=-3:6,samples=2] {(2/3)*x-2};\addplot[only marks,mark=*,mark size=2pt,red] coordinates {(0,-2) (3,0)};\node[blue,above left] at (axis cs:3.6,3.4) {$m=\frac{2}{3}$};\node[red,below right] at (axis cs:4.6,1.1) {$m=\frac{2}{3}$};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
